rationale: The button's only perceivable boundary is its 2px edge; edge #969696 vs page #ffffff is 2.958:1, just under the 3:1 floor, so the component is not visually distinguishable from the page.
citation: "User Interface Components ... Visual information required to identify ... components ... has a contrast ratio of at least 3:1 against the adjacent color(s)." — WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast

rationale: A text input whose only visible boundary is a 1px hairline #999999 vs #ffffff = 2.849:1 (< 3:1); the focusable field's edge does not reach the 3:1 needed to identify it.
citation: "the visual information necessary to identify that a control exists and how to operate it must have a contrast ratio of at least 3:1" — Understanding SC 1.4.11 (Intent)

rationale: The same #767676 edge that is 4.54:1 on white drops to 1.518:1 once the surface flips to the dark card #5a5a5a (button fill matches the card, so the edge is the only boundary) — the theme erodes the only cue below 3:1.
citation: "Graphical Objects ... and the visual information required to identify ... User Interface Components ... at least 3:1 against the adjacent color(s)." — WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11

rationale: A clickable white card (role=button) with no border or shadow; its only boundary is its fill edge #ffffff vs the gray page #e8e8e8 = 1.225:1, so the component boundary is imperceptible.
citation: "The intent of this Success Criterion is to ... make it possible to perceive ... the boundary of a control." — Understanding SC 1.4.11

rationale: The button fill #1a73e8 is 4.5:1 against the white area but only 1.775:1 where it overlaps the blue promo band #0b4ea2; the worst boundary governs, so part of the component's edge is indistinguishable from its adjacent color.
citation: "at least 3:1 against the adjacent color(s)" — the plural 'color(s)' requires every adjacent color to meet 3:1. WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11

rationale: A borderless selectable chip whose identity rests entirely on fill #eeeeee against page #ffffff = 1.160:1; with no edge at all the chip is not perceivable as a component.
citation: "the part(s) of the ... component required to identify it ... must have a contrast ratio of at least 3:1" — Understanding SC 1.4.11 (Intent)

rationale: The author set the only boundary with rgba(0,0,0,0.18); composited over the white page it is #d1d1d1 = 1.527:1, well under 3:1.
citation: "Contrast ratio ... is measured against the adjacent color(s)" — translucent borders are evaluated as composited over their backdrop. Understanding SC 1.4.11

rationale: A segmented control whose internal 1px dividers #cfcfcf on white are 1.558:1; the boundaries that separate the three segments into distinct controls do not reach 3:1, so the segments read as one undifferentiated control.
citation: "Visual information used to indicate ... distinct parts of a control ... requires 3:1 contrast." — Understanding SC 1.4.11 / G195 reasoning

rationale: Dark-theme outline button: fill matches the page, so the #5e5e5e edge is the only boundary; #5e5e5e vs #111111 = 2.912:1, just under 3:1.
citation: "a contrast ratio of at least 3:1 against the adjacent color(s)" — WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11

rationale: The card's only boundary (edge #d9dde2) sits on a CSS gradient backdrop; the deterministic runner cannot reduce the adjacent surface to one flat color and must defer/abstain. The true answer is a barrier (the faint edge melts into the gradient along its whole run).
citation: Trusted Tester 5.1 — 5.1.3 (non-text contrast): "If a boundary cannot be measured against a single adjacent color (gradient/image), determine perceivability by inspection."

rationale: The CTA's only boundary is a near-white outline over a busy repeating pattern (photo stand-in); no flat adjacent color exists so the runner must abstain. Truth: the outline is lost wherever it crosses the light tiles.
citation: "Where the background is not a solid color (e.g. a photographic image), the contrast must be evaluated against the relevant adjacent pixels." — Understanding SC 1.4.11

rationale: A list-row outline #767676 is 4.54:1 on its three white sides but 1.518:1 where its left edge abuts the #5a5a5a sidebar; fully flat/opaque so the runner can decide, and the worst side governs => barrier.
citation: "at least 3:1 against the adjacent color(s)" — every adjacent color must qualify. WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11

rationale: Edge #767676 vs page #ffffff = 4.542:1, well above 3:1; the only boundary is clearly perceivable.
citation: "a contrast ratio of at least 3:1 against the adjacent color(s)" — WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11

rationale: Adversarial near-miss: edge #919191 vs #ffffff = 3.152:1, just OVER 3:1, so it passes; tests that the runner does not over-fire at the boundary.
citation: "at least 3:1" — the threshold is inclusive at 3:1. WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11

rationale: The faint-edged button (#d6d6d6, 1.453:1) is DISABLED; 1.4.11 explicitly exempts inactive/disabled user-interface components, so there is no barrier (an enabled passing button is present as a trap).
citation: "Inactive: A user interface component that is not available for user interaction (e.g., a disabled control in HTML) is not required to meet the contrast requirements." — Understanding SC 1.4.11 (Exceptions)

rationale: The input, select, and submit button carry no author border/background; their boundary is drawn by the browser's default user-agent stylesheet, which 1.4.11 exempts.
citation: "User Agent control: ... the default rendering of a control by the user agent is not author-controlled and is exempt." — Understanding SC 1.4.11 (Exceptions)

rationale: The 1px #e0e0e0 hairline (1.32:1) is not the information required to identify the button; the solid blue fill #1a73e8 vs page #ffffff = 4.5:1 is the perceivable boundary, which passes.
citation: "This requirement applies to the visual information needed to identify ... components ... It does not apply to ... visual information that is not needed." — Understanding SC 1.4.11

rationale: The rgba(0,0,0,0.45) edge composited over the white page is #8c8c8c = 3.363:1, above 3:1; tests that the runner alpha-composites before comparing rather than abstaining on a known flat backdrop.
citation: "Contrast ratio ... measured against the adjacent color(s)" — composited alpha over a flat backdrop is computable. Understanding SC 1.4.11

rationale: The faint #ededed rule (1.171:1) is a decorative separator between prose paragraphs; it is not the boundary of any UI component and bears no information, so it is out of 1.4.11 scope.
citation: "Pure decoration ... is not included in this requirement." — Understanding SC 1.4.11 (and 'decoration' definition)

rationale: Same dark-theme flip structure as the positives, but the author recolored the edge to #8d8d8d for the dark card #1a1a1a, giving 5.244:1; the boundary still passes after the context flip.
citation: "at least 3:1 against the adjacent color(s)" — WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11

rationale: The swatch shows the brand's exact paint color #f3f3f3 (1.11:1 vs page); presenting the true color is essential, and the operable cue is the bordered #767676 frame (4.5:1), so no barrier.
citation: "Essential: A particular presentation of the ... graphical object is essential to the information being conveyed." — Understanding SC 1.4.11 (Exceptions)

rationale: Same gradient backdrop as the abstain positive, but the edge is dark #303030 (>=7:1 against the lightest gradient point), so worst-side still passes; the runner cannot reduce the gradient and should abstain while the truth is PASS.
citation: Trusted Tester 5.1 — 5.1.3: "determine perceivability by inspection where a single adjacent color cannot be measured."

rationale: A heavily rounded pill whose edge is anti-aliased along the curve; a pixel-sampling runner reads blended pixels and should abstain. The author's used colors give #595959 vs #ffffff = 7.0:1, a clear PASS.
citation: "Anti-aliased edges ... should be assessed for the intended foreground/background colors, not the blended boundary pixels." — non-text contrast measurement guidance, Understanding SC 1.4.11

rationale: Borderless chip (same pattern as the positive case-06) whose fill #767676 vs page #ffffff = 4.54:1; with no border the fill is the boundary cue and it passes.
citation: "a contrast ratio of at least 3:1 against the adjacent color(s)" — WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11
